title: Speculative window consolidation + index bloom-hinting to reduce dashboard tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Several dashboard endpoints show high 95/99th percentile latencies for long cursor traversals under multi-tenant workloads. Root causes observed in profiling: (1) repeated small-range index seeks across many partitions when a single logical page contains sparse keys; (2) excessive network roundtrips when clients fetch many small cursor pages; (3) read amplification from tenant-scoped filters that defeat general-purpose page caching.

Proposal: Implement a three-part approach: (A) speculative window consolidation — coalesce adjacent small cursor windows at query time into speculative larger fetches when the cost model predicts fewer backend seeks; (B) per-tenant bloom-hint index summaries — attach compact bloom filters for hot index shards so router can avoid probing shards unlikely to contain matching keys; (C) compact cursor v2 — new cursor encoding that preserves sparse key boundaries and allows server-side partial expansion to avoid roundtrips for commonly accessed follow-on pages.

Goals: reduce read amplification and roundtrips, lower 99th percentile latency for dashboard list queries by >= 30% on heavy multi-tenant traffic, and keep median latency within 5% of baseline.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile tail latency for dashboard list API reduced by >=30% on the reproduced tenant mix
Average backend seeks per client page reduced by >=40% compared to current baseline
No regression on cold-start single-tenant queries (median latency within 5% of baseline)
Automated integration tests for cursor v2 and bloom-hint behavior added to CI
Runbook updated with rollback steps and heuristic tuning knobs
implementation_plan: Design: finalize cost model for speculative consolidation and define thresholds (2 engineer days)
Prototype: implement speculative consolidator in query coordinator behind feature flag (3 days)
Index summaries: generate per-shard bloom-hints in offline job and serve via metadata API (5 days)
Cursor v2: new encoding + server-side partial expansion + backward-compatibility shim (5 days)
Testing: end-to-end perf harness, chaos tests, and canary rollout (4 days)
Rollout: staged traffic ramp with feature flag, monitor metrics and SLOs, iterate on thresholds (2 weeks)
Documentation: update console docs and rollout runbook
risks_and_mitigation: Speculation may fetch too much data and increase bandwidth — mitigate by conservative cost-model and hard caps on consolidation window size
Bloom-hint false positives increase seeks — tune bloom parameters and fall back to probed seek on low-confidence bounds
Cursor v2 incompatibility with old clients — serve compatibility shim and deprecation schedule
Metadata sync lag between index summaries and shards — add TTL and versioning for bloom-hint metadata
